headline: Fractional Marketing Services: Cost, Types & Fit (2026)
description: Fractional marketing services cost $5K-$15K/mo for senior specialists. See types, pricing models, and how to hire the right fractional marketer.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a fractional marketer and a freelancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional marketer takes ongoing ownership of your marketing strategy and results within a specific function. They attend team meetings, set KPIs, and manage campaigns over months. A freelancer typically completes defined tasks or projects — a batch of blog posts, a set of ad creatives — without strategic ownership. Fractional marketers function as part-time team members, not outside vendors.

mainEntity.name: How many hours per week does a fractional marketer work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most fractional marketers work 10-20 hours per week per client. A fractional CMO typically commits 15-20 hours weekly, while channel specialists like SEO experts or paid media buyers often work 10-15 hours. The exact hours depend on scope and are set during engagement setup.

mainEntity.name: Can a fractional marketer replace a full-time CMO?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional CMO can handle strategy, team coordination, and board reporting at 15-20 hours per week, which covers most of what a full-time CMO does. The limitation is availability for real-time decisions and deep company immersion. For companies under $20M in revenue with lean marketing teams, a fractional CMO often delivers 80-90% of the value at 40-50% of the cost.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to hire a fractional marketer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timeline ranges from 48 hours to 2-3 weeks depending on the platform and process. MarketerHire matches companies with vetted marketers within 48 hours. Traditional recruiting or referral-based hiring typically takes 2-4 weeks.

mainEntity.name: What results should I expect from fractional marketing services?

acceptedAnswer.text: Expect measurable progress within the first 30-60 days. For paid channels, that means campaign launches, data collection, and early optimization. For organic channels like SEO or content, expect strategy delivery in month one and measurable traffic movement by month three. Set specific KPIs during onboarding and review them biweekly.
